title: PM Adviser Denies Fixed Deadline for Militia Disarmament Committee
detail: Qasim al-Araji, adviser to PM Ali al-Zaidi and former national security adviser, called reports of a fixed completion deadline for the government's weapons-control committee 'completely incorrect,' saying the September 30 date applies only to the withdrawal of the US-led coalition, not to militia disarmament. Al-Araji warned that anyone caught in illegal possession of weapons going forward would be 'treated as a terrorist.' Three pro-Iran factions — Asaib Ahl al-Haq, Kataib Imam Ali, and Saraya al-Salam — have signaled compliance, while hardliners Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat al-Nujaba continue to refuse disarmament until foreign troops fully depart, with some arguing their weapons originated from Iran and should be returned there rather than surrendered to Baghdad.

media.caption: Iraqi PM adviser Qasim al-Araji says there is no fixed deadline for the militia weapons-control committee

title: Parallel-Market Dollar Tops 160,000 Dinars in Baghdad and Erbil Amid US Treasury Pressure
detail: The US dollar's parallel-market selling rate hit 160,000 IQD per $100 in Baghdad (buying 159,500) and 159,650 in Erbil on Saturday, September 19 — a widening premium over the Central Bank of Iraq's official peg of 131,000 per $100. Traders and analysts linked the surge to heightened US Treasury pressure and tighter restrictions on monthly physical cash shipments from Iraq's oil-revenue reserves held at the Federal Reserve, conditions tied to Baghdad's progress disarming Iran-aligned armed groups. Traders warned rates could reach 170,000 if dollar inflows stay constrained; consumer spending has shifted toward essentials as retail and restaurant traffic declined. The Central Bank says its reserves remain sufficient to meet trade and travel demand at the official rate.

media.caption: Packs of Iraqi dinars at a currency exchange shop in Baghdad

confidenceReason: Reported by a single regional outlet (Iraqi News); not yet corroborated by a Tier-1/Tier-2 wire service, though it is consistent with the widening official/parallel-market spread documented earlier in September.
